To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most effective way to improve the reading speed of TOEIC test takers is to teach them how to recognize and read chunks of words.

1) reading speed is positively correlated with reading comprehension, 2) reading speed is negatively correlated with word-by-word reading, 3) word-by-word reading is negatively correlated with reading comprehension.

the most frequent words in English are also the most useful for reading comprehension, and that these words are best acquired in the form of collocations. (1993) The question of how to go about learning collocations is addressed below.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how much time it takes to read a text.
the acquisition of chunks, which we see as a major part of the process of acquiring a language, and we are concerned with ways of teaching these chunks.
the question of whether the use of a large corpus of authentic language can provide a basis for a rational approach to the teaching and learning of vocabulary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more a learner is familiar with a word, the more likely it will be retrieved from memory, and thus the less effort required to read it.
the more familiar you are with a word, the faster you will read it (Lewis, 2001, p. 2).
the more familiar the student is with the vocabulary, the faster they will read and the more accurately they will understand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vocabulary learning should not be seen as a process of adding isolated words to a mental lexicon, but as a process of learning to recognise and understand chunks of language.
the best approach is one that is both rational and corpus based.
the best way to improve vocabulary is to read a lot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more a reader knows about a text, the faster they can read it.
vocabulary is not just words, but chunks of words.
the more words you have in your vocabulary, the faster you read.
